title: Turn out the Lights, Turn up the Stars

context_sources.name: Light pollution map
context_sources.role: Artificial light intensity and sky brightness

context_sources.name: Google Trends
context_sources.role: Search counts used as the publicity indicator

context_sources.name: Falchi et al. 2016
context_sources.role: The world atlas cited for the 80 percent figure

limitations: Equations 1 to 19 print as bare numbers with the symbols stripped.
The notation table lists descriptions with no symbols.
The four site tables scramble several values across rows.
The recomputed indices under each strategy are never printed.
Page 25, the flyer, has no text layer and was read from the page image.

tasks: Build a broadly applicable light pollution metric and grade locations with it
Apply it to a protected, rural, suburban, and urban location
Propose three intervention strategies and their actions
Find the best strategy for two locations and publish a flyer

section_map.summary: Four indices from 35.55 to 84.18 and a win for cutting the light.
The 1950s origin, the 80 percent figure, and the 7,000-star contrast.
A higher index means cleaner, weak factors are dropped, and the data are trusted.
Ten indicators under light, society, and nature, blended into one index.
Hierarchy, entropy, and variation weights averaged.
New York, Bellevue, Sedona, and Yellowstone graded I through IV.
Less light, more publicity, and more vegetation, traced by three networks.
Cutting the light wins for both Sedona and New York at a ten percent dose.
Dropping light density leaves the other curves almost unchanged.
Three steps for New York: light only where needed, warm LEDs, shielded downlighting.

contributions.summary: Three weighting methods are averaged so none decides alone.
The index is defined to rise as the night gets cleaner, and the choice is justified.
Direct effects are separated from effects that travel through correlation.
The strategies are compared at an equal ten percent dose.

dependency_graph.handoff: The averaged weights enter the three group scores and the index.
The ten indicators and their correlations decide what each network predicts.
The networks supply the indirect indicators that the rescoring needs.

assumptions.summary: A higher index means a lower level of light pollution.
Factors with weak correlation are removed.
Data from official sites are true and reliable.
A ten percent change is a fair common dose for all three strategies.
Correlations estimated on fifty-five sites hold inside one city.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Light intensity and sky brightness taken from the Light Pollution Map.
Publicity measured by Google Trends searches for light pollution.
Transparency and humidity taken from the national weather service and standardized.
Green area and species counts taken from each country's forestry service.

models.summary: Scores a site from light, society, and nature and grades it in four bands.
Averages a hierarchy weight, an entropy weight, and a variation weight.
Traces each direct action through Spearman correlation and a neural network.
Picks the strategy that lifts the index most at an equal dose.

verification.summary: New York's grade I is checked against its density, skyglow, and late nights.
Yellowstone's grade IV is checked against its own lighting rules.
Normality is tested before Spearman correlation is chosen.
Rebuilding the network without light density leaves the curves nearly unchanged.

results_trace.summary: New York 35.55, grade I, heavy pollution.
Cutting artificial light wins for both Sedona and New York, though New York stays in grade I.

writing_logic.summary: Count the indicators, the regions, and the groups before naming the model.
Date the problem and give the global share before the local one.
Follow every assumption with its justification.
Warn that the obvious link may run backward.
Say what is subjective and what is sensitive before blending them.
Test normality before choosing the coefficient.
Hold the effort equal before comparing the strategies.
Report a win that does not change the grade.

language_observations.summary: The index direction is justified by the habit of giving better conditions higher scores.
The paper calls its own formula extremely creative.
Each grade is matched to a kind of place, from a city center to a national park.
Each plotted curve is translated into sleep, safety, or wildlife.
The flyer opens by asking the reader when they last saw stars.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1 flowcharts the whole paper from the index to the flyer.
Figure 2 draws the evaluation system with three groups and ten indicators.
Figure 3 draws the hierarchy used for the judgment matrices.
Figure 4 plots the combined weight of each indicator.
Tables 3 to 7 give the raw data for the four sites.
Figure 5 plots the three network trends, one panel per strategy.
Figure 6 compares the three strategies for Sedona.
Figure 7 compares the three strategies for New York.
Figure 8 overlays the original and the reduced network on three indicators.
Table 2 sets the four grades against the cuts at 40, 60, and 80.
Table 1 lists the notation with the symbols missing.
The flyer asks when the reader last saw stars and gives three numbered steps.
The flyer cites 80 percent of the world and 50 percent of city sleep.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge rewards averaging a subjective weight with two objective ones.
A judge rewards comparing strategies at an equal dose.
A judge penalizes a ranking whose recomputed indices are never shown.

weaknesses.summary: The notation table prints descriptions with the symbols stripped.
Equations 1 to 19 print as bare numbers.
The site tables scramble values across rows.
The odd positive correlation between biodiversity and sky brightness is not explained.
No neuron count or training error is given.
The recomputed indices are never printed.
The model is once called the LNS system.
The same atlas is cited twice.

independent_extensions.statement: Print the recomputed index for each site under each strategy and check that the ranking survives.
independent_extensions.reason: The paper reports only which strategy wins, so the size of the gain is unknown.

independent_extensions.statement: Price the three strategies and repeat the comparison per unit of cost.
independent_extensions.reason: An equal ten percent move is treated as an equal effort, which the paper never checks.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Supports tracing an intervention through correlation into a network before rescoring.
Supports comparing interventions at an equal dose and keeping the one aimed at the heaviest indicator.

unresolved_questions: What index each site reaches under each strategy.
What neuron counts and training errors the three networks had.
Why biodiversity correlates positively with sky brightness.
